He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]], earning consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in his junior season. The [[Chicago Bulls]] selected him with the 38th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Ayo Dosunmu was born in [[Chicago]] to a [[Nigerians|Nigerian]] father and [[African Americans|African American]] mother. His father descends from the [[Yoruba people]] in Nigeria, and his name Ayo means "joy" in the [[Yoruba language]]. Dosunmu began his high school career at Chicago's [[George Westinghouse College Prep|Westinghouse College Prep]], where he helped lead the Warriors to a 2015 conference championship against Al Raby High School and scored a season-high 40 points against Crane High School as a freshman,{{Cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2016/4/8/18490109/michael-o-8217-brien-8217-s-notebook-april-8-2016|title=Michael O'Brien's notebook: April 8, 2016|date=8 April 2016}}{{Cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-saturday/2019/5/11/18619086/from-chicago-with-joy-ayo-dosunmu-s-name-and-game-are-fueling-illini-rise|title = From Chicago, with Joy: Ayo Dosunmu's name — and game — are fueling Illini rise|date = 11 May 2019}} earning ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' All-City Accolades. Dosunmu transferred after his freshman year to [[Morgan Park High School|Morgan Park]]. During his junior year, Dosunmu led the Mustangs to a 3A State Championship, although he was unable to play in the championship game due to injury. In his senior year, Dosunmu led the Mustangs once again to a state championship, in which he scored 28 points; breaking an [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] record for points scored in a championship game. In March 2018, Dosunmu was named one of 26 high school seniors who participated in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] on April 8, 2018, at the [[Barclays Center]] in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City|New York]].{{cite web | url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/mens-basketball/2018-03-08/ayo-play-jordan-brand-classic.html | title=Ayo to play in Jordan Brand Classic | publisher=News-Gazette | date=March 8, 2018 | access-date=April 4, 2018}} Dosunmu is the third Illini to be selected to play in the Jordan Classic, joining [[Dee Brown (basketball, born 1984)|Dee url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/daily-southtown/sports/ct-sta-boys-basketball-morgan-park-springfield-southeast-st-0318-20180317-story.html | title=Illinois recruit Ayo Dosunmu leads Morgan
